title_en: Qingdao Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., Ltd. v. Gangrun (Liaocheng) Printing and Dyeing Co., Ltd. — dispute over right of repossession
ruling_gist_en: Article 23 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China provides: 'The creation and transfer of property rights in movables shall take effect upon delivery, except as otherwise provided by law.' Meanwhile, Article 27 of the same Law provides: 'Where the parties agree that the transferor continues to possess the chattel when the property right in a chattel is transferred, the property right shall take effect when the agreement becomes effective.' Pursuant to the above provisions, the transfer of property rights in movables takes delivery as the element of publicity, regardless of whether the method of delivery is actual delivery or delivery by way of constructive delivery (possession by agreement). If the parties merely reach an agreement on the transfer of the property right but do not enter into an agreement that the transferor continues to possess the chattel (a constructive delivery agreement), it cannot constitute constructive delivery as provided in Article 27 of the Property Law, and therefore cannot effect the transfer of the property right.

full_text_en:
Qingdao Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., Ltd. v. Gangrun (Liaocheng) Printing and Dyeing Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Confirmation of Right of Recovery

【Ruling Summary】

Article 23 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The creation and transfer of real rights in movables shall take effect upon delivery, unless otherwise provided by law." At the same time, Article 27 of the said Law provides: "Where, at the time of transfer of a real right in a movable, the parties agree that the transferor shall continue to possess the movable, the real right shall take effect upon the effectiveness of such agreement." According to the above provisions, the transfer of a real right in a movable requires delivery as an element of public notice, regardless of whether the method of delivery is actual delivery or delivery by means of a constitution possessorium. If the parties have only reached an agreement on the transfer of the real right but have not reached an agreement on the transferor's continued possession of the movable by means of a constitution possessorium, this does not constitute a constitution possessorium as provided in Article 27 of the Property Law, and therefore, the effect of the transfer of the real right cannot take place.

Plaintiff: Qingdao Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., Ltd. Domicile: Jiaoxi Town, Jiaozhou City, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Defendant: Gangrun (Liaocheng) Printing and Dyeing Co., Ltd. (Bankruptcy Liquidation). Domicile: Huangshan North Road, Development Zone, Liaocheng City, Shandong Province.

Third Party: Qingdao Chengquan Fabric Co., Ltd. Domicile: Jiaoxi Town, Jiaozhou City, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

The Plaintiff, Qingdao Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.), filed a lawsuit with the Jiaozhou City People's Court of Shandong Province on April 12, 2010, regarding a dispute over the confirmation of the right of recovery against Gangrun (Liaocheng) Printing and Dyeing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co.). On May 24, 2010, the Jiaozhou City People's Court of Shandong Province ruled to transfer the case to the Intermediate People's Court of Liaocheng City, Shandong Province for trial.

The Plaintiff, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., alleged: Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. and the Third Party, Qingdao Chengquan Fabric Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chengquan Fabric Co.), supplied fabric to the Defendant, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. As of November 4, 2009, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. owed Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. RMB 1,195,139.17 for fabric products and owed Chengquan Fabric Co. RMB 1,075,952.31. On November 20, 2009, the three parties consulted and reached an agreement whereby Chengquan Fabric Co. transferred all its accounts receivable to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., and Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. agreed to offset the outstanding debts with seven pieces of its mechanical equipment. The ownership of the seven pieces of equipment was to be transferred to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. upon the signing of the agreement. However, after the delivery date agreed upon in the agreement passed, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. did not perform in accordance with the agreement. The Plaintiff requested: 1. To confirm that the ownership of the seven pieces of equipment of Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. belongs to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.; 2. To order Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. to deliver the seven pieces of equipment to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.; 3. The litigation costs to be borne by Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co.

The Defendant, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co., argued: Although Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. had signed an agreement with the Plaintiff, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., stipulating that the ownership of the equipment in question would be transferred to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., since there was no actual delivery, the ownership of the equipment did not transfer. Therefore, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.'s request should not be granted. Since the ownership of the equipment did not transfer, according to the Bankruptcy Law, the equipment still belongs to the bankruptcy estate and should not be delivered to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. Furthermore, after Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. entered bankruptcy proceedings, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. had already declared its claim, indicating its recognition that the right it holds is a bankruptcy claim, not ownership of the equipment. In summary, the Defendant requested that Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.'s claims be dismissed in accordance with the law.

The Third Party, Chengquan Fabric Co., stated: It acknowledges the fact of the assignment of the claim as asserted by the Plaintiff, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.

Facts Found by the Intermediate People's Court of Liaocheng City, Shandong Province at First Instance:

The Plaintiff, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., and the Third Party, Chengquan Fabric Co., supplied fabric to the Defendant, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. As of November 4, 2009, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. owed Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. RMB 1,195,139.17 and owed Chengquan Fabric Co. RMB 1,075,952.31. On November 20, 2009, the three companies reached the following agreement: 1. Chengquan Fabric Co. would transfer all of Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co.'s outstanding debts to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., and both Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. and Chengquan Fabric Co. agreed that Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. would directly pay the debt to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. 2. Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. agreed that Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. would offset the outstanding debts with seven pieces of its mechanical equipment, and the ownership of these seven pieces of equipment would be transferred to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. from the effective date of this agreement. 3. Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. should deliver the equipment used for offset to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. before March 31, 2010, and ensure that Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. takes possession of the equipment smoothly. Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. must strictly deliver the equipment within the aforementioned timeframe; if delivery is delayed, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. shall pay a late payment penalty to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. at a daily rate of one-thousandth of the total outstanding debt amount. After the agreement was signed, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. did not deliver the seven pieces of equipment to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. before the agreed date of March 31, 2010.

On March 17, 2010, the Intermediate People's Court of Liaocheng City, Shandong Province, rendered a civil ruling accepting the bankruptcy application filed by Hengrun Thermal Power Company against the Defendant, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. On May 6, 2010, the Plaintiff, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., declared its claim to Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. On July 27, 2010, the Intermediate People's Court of Liaocheng City rendered a civil ruling declaring Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. bankrupt.

Judgment of the Intermediate People's Court of Liaocheng City, Shandong Province at First Instance:

The court held that the tripartite agreement signed by the Plaintiff, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., the Defendant, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co., and the Third Party, Chengquan Fabric Co., was lawful and valid. However, the validity of the agreement does not mean that the real right in the seven pieces of equipment in question was transferred. Article 23 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The creation and transfer of real rights in movables shall take effect upon delivery, unless otherwise provided by law." This provision excludes agreements between the parties. In this case, although the parties agreed that the ownership of the seven pieces of equipment would be transferred to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. from the effective date of this agreement, the equipment was not delivered to Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., and the situation did not fall within the three exceptions provided in the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, namely, constitution possessorium, delivery by instruction, or simplified delivery. Therefore, the real right in the seven pieces of equipment was not transferred due to non-delivery. Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. is not the owner of the seven pieces of equipment in question but rather a creditor of Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. Since Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. was declared bankrupt, the seven pieces of equipment in question are part of the bankruptcy estate of Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co.

In conclusion, the Intermediate People's Court of Liaocheng City, Shandong Province, in accordance with Article 23 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 107, Paragraph 2 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 3, 2010:

The claims of the Plaintiff, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., are dismissed.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 28,776 shall be borne by the Plaintiff, Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.

Yuanhongxiang Textile Co., dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the High People's Court of Shandong Province, arguing: 1. According to Article 23 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, "The creation and transfer of real rights in movables shall take effect upon delivery, unless otherwise provided by law." However, Article 133 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The ownership of the subject matter shall be transferred upon delivery, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties." Furthermore, according to Article 27 of the Property Law, "Where, at the time of transfer of a real right in a movable, the parties agree that the transferor shall continue to possess the movable, the real right shall take effect upon the effectiveness of such agreement." In this case, the agreement took effect on November 20, 2009. The parties agreed that the ownership of the seven pieces of equipment would be transferred to the Appellant from the effective date of this agreement and also agreed that the transferor, i.e., the Appellee Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co., would continue to possess the seven pieces of equipment. Therefore, the delivery date for the seven pieces of equipment was November 20, 2009. According to Article 27 of the Property Law regarding constitution possessorium, the first-instance court erred in finding that the ownership of the seven pieces of equipment belonged to the bankruptcy estate of Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. The Appellant requested that the second-instance court reverse the original judgment and render a fair judgment.

The Appellee, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co., responded: 1. Regarding the change in ownership of movables, the Contract Law takes delivery as the principle, with legal provisions and party agreements as exceptions, while the newer Property Law takes delivery as the principle, with special legal provisions as exceptions, thereby excluding party agreements. 2. The creation and transfer of real rights in movables follow the principle of no effect without delivery, and the act of delivery must be in the form prescribed by law. Neither Article 2 nor Article 3 of the agreement in question constitutes a "constitution possessorium"; rather, they stipulate that the Appellee, Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co., should deliver by a certain time. Therefore, the Appellant Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.'s grounds for appeal are untenable and should be dismissed.

The original trial Third Party, Chengquan Fabric Co., stated: It agrees with the Appellant Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.'s opinions in the appeal.

The High People's Court of Shandong Province, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The disputed issue in this case is whether the delivery of the equipment in question was completed, i.e., whether the ownership of the equipment in question had been transferred.

Reasoning of the High People's Court of Shandong Province at Second Instance:

First, the seven pieces of equipment in question are movables, and the principle of public notice for movables is possession and delivery. Article 6 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The creation and transfer of real rights in movables shall be delivered in accordance with the law." So-called delivery refers to the transfer of possession, i.e., the act of transferring the possession of an object or a title certificate from oneself to another person. Article 23 of the Property Law provides: "The creation and transfer of real rights in movables shall take effect upon delivery, unless otherwise provided by law." It can be seen that, for the sake of maintaining transaction security, delivery, as the statutory method for the change of real rights in movables, is mandatory. The said Law provides for four methods of delivery: actual delivery, simplified delivery, delivery by instruction, and constitution possessorium. Article 133 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The ownership of the subject matter shall be transferred upon delivery, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties." This provision also takes delivery as the effective condition for the change of real rights in movables, and the content covered by "unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties" refers to constructive delivery methods other than actual delivery as provided by other laws. The subsequently implemented Property Law further clarified that the parties can only choose a specific delivery method by agreement among the four delivery methods provided by law; apart from this, there is no other method for the change of real rights in movables based on legal acts.

Second, regarding whether the method agreed upon in the agreement in question constitutes a constitution possessorium. A constitution possessorium refers to a situation where, after the transferor and the transferee reach an agreement on the change of a real right in a movable, the transferor continues to possess the movable in accordance with a contract concluded between them, thereby allowing the transferee to obtain indirect possession, replacing actual delivery. Article 27 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where, at the time of transfer of a real right in a movable, the parties agree that the transferor shall continue to possess the movable, the real right shall take effect upon the effectiveness of such agreement." From the above provision, it can be derived that the constitutive elements of a constitution possessorium are: (1) The parties reach an agreement on the change of the real right in a movable. This agreement is the basis for delivery; (2) In addition to reaching the agreement on the change of the real right, the parties reach a separate agreement regarding the movable that the transferor will continue to possess and use the movable. In this case, although the agreement on the transfer of real rights in the seven pieces of equipment signed by the parties contained content regarding the change of ownership, there was no separate agreement reached between the parties regarding the Appellee Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co.'s continued possession and use of the seven pieces of equipment. Therefore, the agreement between Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. and the Appellant Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. does not constitute a delivery by means of a constitution possessorium.

In summary, since the seven pieces of equipment were not actually delivered, although the agreement signed by the parties is valid, it only creates an obligatory effect and does not produce the effect of a change in real rights. The Appellant Yuanhongxiang Textile Co. did not actually obtain ownership of the seven pieces of equipment, and therefore, it does not have the right of recovery in the bankruptcy case of the Appellee Gangrun Printing and Dyeing Co. The Appellant Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.'s argument that the real rights in the seven pieces of equipment in question were transferred to it through the tripartite agreement and that it has the right of recovery for such equipment is untenable.

Accordingly, the High People's Court of Shandong Province, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on May 5, 2011:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 28,776 shall be borne by the Appellant Yuanhongxiang Textile Co.
